correctness.rationale: Verified the projector identity and reconstructed the extrema. The t-derivative of the z^k coefficient of det(I+zA(I+tyyᵀ)Aᵀ) sums w_S yᵀP_Sy over full-rank blocks; singular blocks have identically zero determinant. On the Gram eigenbasis this coefficient is the quadratic form with diagonal λ_i e_{k−1}(λ_{−i}), and the normalizer is e_k(λ). Pairwise subtraction gives p_j−p_i=(λ_j−λ_i)e_{k−1}(λ_{−i,−j})/e_k(λ), strictly reflecting ordering when k<N and the eigenvalues differ. At endpoints 1 and κ, μ=1/(1+e_k(κ,u)/e_{k−1}(κ,u)) decreases in the intermediate entries u. The condition ratio is κ(t+1)/(t+κ), with t=e_{k−1}(u)/e_{k−2}(u) increasing in u. For an exposed coordinate, the derivative of each consecutive symmetric ratio has numerator b²−ac for successive coefficients a,b,c; normalized Newton is strict when both neighbors are positive, and if one is zero the numerator is b²>0 in the interior k range. Evaluating u≡1 or u≡κ gives the four bounds and shows uniqueness of the interior spectral profiles, not of the matrices. For a prescribed rectangular m, pad the attaining diagonal A by zero rows, which have zero sampling weight. At k=1, F=B/tr B; at k=N, F=I; at κ=1, F=(k/N)I. The projection Pythagorean identity yields worst factor 1−μ, with the sharp ceiling threshold obtained by solving the monotone inequality in k, including δ=1.
residual_risks: Checks of integer spectra and rotating numerical examples are supplementary. The claim does not address inconsistent systems, approximate sampling, or adaptive multistep optimality.

evidence: Xiang et al. give a spectrum-dependent rate with floor σ_min²/(σ_k²+⋯+σ_min²) for a size-k block, and Rodomanov–Kropotov bound their related inverse expectation via a spectrum-dependent coordinate approximation.
broader_coverage.reasoning: On (1,κ,…,κ) the Xiang floor is 1/[1+(N−k)κ], strictly below the frozen k/[k+(N−k)κ] when 1<k<N. Although the form can exceed the uniform floor on some individual spectra, it is not a dominating sharp condition-only envelope, and it does not supply either opposite bound.

evidence: The indexed proof writes p₁=1/(1+e_k(λ₂,…,λ_N)/e_{k−1}(λ₂,…,λ_N)), proves the derivative sign for every positive coordinate via Newton, and invokes strict positivity for k<N.

It also writes χ=h(s+1)/(s+h) for h=λ_N and s=e_{k−1}(T)/e_{k−2}(T), with T the intermediate spectrum, and proves s is coordinatewise nondecreasing and the outer function is strictly increasing for h>1.
Its lower μ already supplies the same worst conditional rate and sharp cutoff.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Restrict the indexed condition-at-most setting to h=κ. The proven monotonicities put the maximum p₁ and minimum χ at T=(1,…,1). There s=(N−k)/(k−1) for 2≤k<N; evaluating gives exactly κ(N−1)/(N−k+(k−1)κ) for χ, and e_{k−1}(κ,T)/e_k(1,κ,T) gives the advertised upper μ. The same exposed-coordinate Newton derivative is strictly positive when applicable, so it also forces the claimed unique interior alternate profile. k=1 and k=N use the existing boundary identities. No new optimization step remains.
